novel_mechanics_found: ACTION1/ACTION2 move the anchored arm vertically and ACTION4/ACTION3 extend/retract it. The two banked levels register colored encounters through arm positioning, but level 2 introduces a vertically connected color stack plus a maroon node; the earlier horizontal/independent-target strategy does not carry over directly.
narrative: The 44-action banked prefix was recovered through the resolver and repeatedly confirmed at frame.levels_completed == 2. I traced the prefix frame by frame to infer the arm controls, then explored the vertical connected layout using clean resets, HUD-order and reverse-order encounters, exact-edge and full-boundary extensions, full retractions, direct interaction with the maroon/connector glyph, and ACTION5/ACTION6 coordinate probes. None advanced frame.levels_completed beyond 2, so I stopped at the genuine level-2 mechanic wall with budget reserved for verification. A fresh-reset reproduce() gate replayed the stored 44-action sequence and passed claimed_level=2.
gotchas: An extended arm can block vertical movement when it intersects a colored object, so apparent no-op moves are collision-dependent.
Crossing a colored sprite transiently changes its matching HUD icon pixels, but that visual overlap is not evidence that the level accepted the interaction.
The long 2-to-3 bar is action-budget/timing-like UI state and changes on otherwise harmless actions.
ACTION5 and ACTION6 were no-ops both without data and with coordinates on the maroon node and HUD objects.
The maroon 2x2 node and the 2/3 connector beneath it are new at level 2; direct clicking and attempted arm alignment did not reveal their role.
